npu-computing-forecast.title: Ascend NPU Resource Prediction
npu-computing-forecast.summary: An industry collaboration on reproducible experiments, monitoring, and resource prediction for recommendation and language models on Ascend NPUs, supporting workload co-location and better cluster utilization.

images.dataOrderAllocatorComparison: Memory comparison across data orders and allocator settings
images.trainingResourceDistribution: 3D distribution of training configurations and resource usage
images.configurationCoverageDistribution: Model and NPU-count coverage with fine-tuning method distribution

projectIntro: **Training and inference resource analysis**: Studies how task configuration, model structure, and data features can predict hardware usage, TTFT, TPOT, and KV cache for recommendation and language models.
**Evidence from real workloads**: Observes resource and performance behavior on Ascend NPUs, builds familiarity with the hardware and software ecosystem, and reports firsthand issues to the partner.
personalWork: **Experimental data pipeline**: Independently built a configuration-driven pipeline for workload execution, metric collection, data processing, and analysis. Supported batch and repeated experiments with consistent logging and configuration/result retention, providing reproducible data for performance diagnosis and resource prediction. Adapted TorchRec, DeepCTR, Torch-RecHub, and RecSDK, then extended it to LLaMA Factory fine-tuning, vLLM inference, and multiple NPUs.

**Reliability in AI-assisted experiments**: Recognized that AI-written settings could be silently ignored by the experiment framework. Designed and implemented strict configuration validation to reject unknown settings, together with checks that parameters actually take effect, rather than treating a written configuration as proof of execution.

**From observation to diagnosis**: Tracked workload behavior and reported issues to the partner, including slow first epochs in DLRM and reserved-memory fluctuations. After observing the memory fluctuations, designed experiments on input order and allocator settings, distinguished active from reserved memory, traced the effect of variable-length inputs, and validated expandable segments across models and tuning methods.

**Trustworthy measurement**: Collected NPU, CPU, and memory metrics through DCMI, cgroup, and related interfaces, preserving raw traces for analysis and feature extraction. Aligned per-rank events with resource traces, separated initialization from training, and cross-checked measurements with npu-smi, npu-exporter, vmstat, lxcfs, and sar.

**Resource modeling and feature design**: Used XGBoost with pre-run features from task configuration, model structure, and data distributions, comparing feature sets, data splits, direct memory prediction, and corrections to static estimates. Built an interim Llama fine-tuning resource predictor on 1,031 runs across 1B/3B/8B/70B models, using 43 features to predict 20 metrics covering peak per-device HBM usage, AI Core/Vector Core utilization, HBM bandwidth utilization, and power over full-observation and shared training windows. On 206 runs held out by configuration group, mean R² over 20 targets was 0.976, with individual target scores of 0.922–0.992 across the full test set.

crater.title: Crater Heterogeneous AI Platform
crater.summary: RAIDS Lab's Kubernetes platform for shared AI clusters, unifying scheduling, development environments, training and serving, images, data, and resource governance.

images.backendLogDiagnostics: Backend logs and slow SQL diagnostics

projectIntro: **Deployment and adoption**: The lab deployment serves 600+ students and faculty with 280+ accelerators, 5,600+ CPU cores, and 200+ jobs created daily. Multiple companies have adopted the platform and proposed collaborations; some components are National Key R&D Program deliverables.

**Shared resource governance**: Combines a custom admission controller with Volcano scheduling, account quotas, queueing and backfilling, CephFS space limits, and bandwidth controls. A migration to Volcano extender integration is planned.
**Resource misuse detection**: Identifies scripts that reserve GPUs for long periods without doing meaningful work, helping curb resource hoarding.
**Unified platform access**: Replaces the lab’s Slurm tooling with a web console and supports systems research in scheduling and distributed storage.
**Reusable environments and data**: Provides snapshots, Buildx and Envd image builds, NFS and Ceph storage, and model and dataset download management.
**Automated user support**: An embedded Q&A agent is largely implemented to help users find information and troubleshoot platform issues.
personalWork: **Turning user needs into delivery**: Translated frontline feedback into features and fixes, improving workflows and error messages. Designed and built the Crater CLI framework and Agent Skills from scratch for people, scripts, and AI agents.

**Technical judgment and review**: Ranked fourth among the project's 26 human developers. As a core maintainer, contributed to planning and design reviews. Used AI to study mechanisms I did not yet understand, formed my own understanding, and brought that judgment into 40+ PR reviews. Wrote technical posts and mentored new contributors through delivery.

**Production diagnosis**: Identified root causes and helped drive fixes for RDMA device detection, CephFS faults, job slowdowns caused by the platform, container startup failures, and cluster egress issues.

**Quality assurance mechanisms**: Codified my quality judgment and experience in Skills covering development, review, documentation, and releases. Made engineering constraints, verification steps, and review requirements reusable across the team, helping contributors use AI reliably and keep the platform maintainable.
**Usable development environments**: Built and refined Jupyter, CUDA, and PyTorch images early in the project, adapting them to the platform and simplifying first use and environment setup.

**Platform features and engineering**: Added Dockerfile generation from dependencies and builds from submitted Dockerfiles. Improved Jupyter startup, user permissions, SSH, initialization hooks, account membership and role changes, user job lists, and visibility into node workload ownership and IPs. Integrated LDAP/AD and removed lab-specific service dependencies. Handled job template migrations, node selection, and stale RDMA settings, and strengthened CLI authentication, completion, compatibility diagnostics, cross-platform distribution, CI, configuration management, and version tracking, among other improvements.

crater-cli.title: Crater CLI
crater-cli.summary: A Go CLI subproject for operating Crater through AI agents, scripts, and related workflows.

projectIntro: **More ways to operate Crater**: Gives command-line users, scripts, and AI agents an entry point that complements the web interface.
**Growing API coverage**: Gradually connects Crater module APIs to expand the operations available through the CLI.
personalWork: **Interface and architecture design**: Designed the CLI from scratch around people, scripts, and AI agents. Added non-interactive operation, structured output, defined error codes, and accompanying Skills for automation and troubleshooting.

**Verifiable delivery**: Isolated network and storage access in a sandbox so tests leave real environments and cluster data untouched. Combined unit tests with golden snapshots so reviewers can inspect command output and later AI development has concrete examples.

**AI collaboration practices**: Maintained architecture, specification, command, and review documents to guide implementation through explicit contracts and verification requirements, recording engineering decisions and trade-offs.
**Usable command-line interaction**: Provided multilingual Tab completion across shells and survey-style prompts, balancing human convenience with predictable automated use.

model-requirements-evaluator.title: Equivalent Modeling and Evaluation of Model Compute Requirements
model-requirements-evaluator.summary: Models inference-time resource requirements for LLMs across vendors' hardware. Given a model, GPU, concurrency, and latency needs, it produces deployment plans that satisfy the constraints.

projectIntro: **Competition recognition**: Won third prize in the 2nd “China Data Valley Huawei Cup” China Graduate Operating System Open Source Innovation Competition.
**Model resource analysis**: Decomposes language model structure and mathematically models the storage and compute requirements of each component.
personalWork: **Turning backend capabilities into a product**: Built an interactive frontend with Vue 3, TypeScript, Vite, and Element Plus for exploring model resource estimates.

**Visualization for informed decisions**: Used ECharts and ECharts-GL to show latency, throughput, memory, and phase progress, helping users connect model structure and inference stages with resource demand and understand how changing requirements affect deployment cost.

personal-homepage.title: Personal Homepage and Content System
personal-homepage.summary: This site is also a long-running frontend project for HR, interviewers, open-source peers, and students. It organizes job-search presentation, open-source activity, and related content into a maintainable static site.

projectIntro: **Designing across viewing conditions**: Adapted layouts to phones and varied desktop sizes, with multiple languages, themes, and animation levels. Dimmed bright screenshots in dark mode to keep reading comfortable.
**Consistent long-term iteration**: Maintained AI instructions and project specifications that capture goals, design principles, and constraints for future changes.

**Integrating generated media into a product**: Generated line art, theme concepts, and video with AI, then recovered the camera path for the homepage FPV sequence. Kept copy, language, and theme in the site so content changes do not require a new video, building practical experience in media integration.
**Reusable content architecture**: Separated presentation from content so components can render different entries and one entry can serve several pages, simplifying maintenance and extension.

images.yolov8ThroughputPrediction: YOLOv8 GPU compute throughput utilization prediction capability

projectIntro: **Modeling execution behavior**: Mapped ONNX operators to GPU kernel sequences, built kernel-level computation graphs, and studied the factors that affect those mappings.

**Low-cost prediction and evaluation**: Built rule-based models to predict the kernels used by ONNX operators and estimate compute and memory usage. Evaluated predictions as groundwork for later interference analysis and scheduling.
**Automated experimentation**: Built tools for batch profiling, trace parsing, and Nsight Compute data integration, supporting mapping analysis, rule construction, and visualization.
